newsitem.title: USA: Hortense drifts toward Puerto Rico, then Dominican.
newsitem.headline: Hortense drifts toward Puerto Rico, then Dominican.

text.p: A hurricane warning remained in effect for Puerto Rico and a tropical storm warning was in effect for the U.S. and British Virgin Islands Monday as Hurricane Hortense continued to drift slowly northwestward, National Hurricane Center said.
A hurricane watch also was in effect for the south coast of Dominican Republic from Cabo Engano to the Haitian border.
At 1400 EDT/1800 GMT, Hortense's center was near latitude 16.5 north and longitude 65.3 west -- about 130 miles (210 km) southeast of Ponce, Puerto Rico.
Maximum sustained winds were near 80 mph (130 kmh) and soe strengthening was likely during the next 24 hours.

The storm was drifting slowly northwestward, but was expected to resume a west to west-northwest motion Monday. Hurricane force winds extended outward up to 60 miles (95 km) from the center and tropical storm force winds etended outward up to 175 miles (280 km).

Rainfall totals of up to 12 inches (30 cm) or even higher were possible along the path of the slow-moving storm, carrying the risk, of life-threatening flash floods and mud slides over mountainous terrain.
Forecasters also said strong on-shore winds could produce storm surge flooding along Puerto Rico's south coast.
